newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: BAESA denies report on risk to debt deal.
newsitem.headline: BAESA denies report on risk to debt deal.

text.p: Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), Pepsi Co's biggest bottler outside the United States, on Friday denied a news report that it could not meet its debt obligations and is considering filing for protection from creditors.
"It is not true that it is analyzing filing for protection from creditors," the firm's Director Enrique Garrido told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange in a letter.
He said statements attributed to a company official in a news service report published Friday were innacurate.

Garrido's letter said BAESA is still talking with leading creditors in the framework of a "standstill agreement" signed last year. Under that agreement, BAESA agreed to defer until March 31 repayments of capital of about $520 million.

The account published in Clarin newspaper reported that BAESA Director for Corporate Planning Carlos Fava said "without a restructuring agreement the company can't meet its obligations" and "the most probable option" was a reorganization of debt along the lines of the local equivalent to Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.

The firm has said the agreement and financial support from Pepsi, which has operating control over BAESA, allowed it to reverse operating difficulties that had caused large losses although it acknowledged it was still in a "delicate situation."
In July Pepsi took over operating control of BAESA, which has suffered a financial crunch that many analysts blame on overexpansion.
In fiscal 1996 BAESA lost $452.4 million versus a $44.8 million gain in 1995.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and certain Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
